title: Baja Fish Tacos
kicker: Beer-battered fish, cabbage crunch, lime crema — invented by Japanese immigrants in Baja, perfected by everyone since.
story: The fish taco story runs through Ensenada and San Felipe, where Japanese immigrants introduced tempura-style frying to local catch in the 1950s. The result is its own thing: strips of white fish in a light beer batter, tucked into warm tortillas with shredded cabbage, pico de gallo, and a lime-heavy crema — street food with a seafood counter's soul.

Three textures must survive the trip to your mouth: shattering batter, flaky fish, cabbage snap. So the batter stays cold (ice-cold beer, no overmixing — lumps are fine, gluten is not), the oil stays at 190°C / 375°F, and the cabbage gets salted and lime-dressed just before serving. The crema is mayonnaise, Mexican crema and lime whisked loose. Nothing exotic; everything in balance.
fun_fact: Baja fish tacos stayed a regional secret until the 1980s, when a Surfer magazine writer ate them in Ensenada and wrote them up — the surf-food pipeline brought them to California and then everywhere.

ingredients.note: cod, pollock, or whatever is flaky and local
green or a mix with red

ingredients.item: mayonnaise + 3 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream

ingredients.note: one for crema, one at the table
diced tomato, onion, chili, lime, cilantro

steps.title: Prep the slaw and crema
steps.text: Toss cabbage with a pinch of salt, squeeze of lime and cilantro; rest 15 minutes, then drain any puddle. Whisk mayo, crema, lime juice and a pinch of salt until pourable.

steps.title: Cut and dry the fish
steps.text: Cut fillets into 2 cm strips. Pat bone-dry — wet fish makes wet batter slide off. Dust lightly with flour; the batter grips dusted fish.

steps.title: Cold batter, fast mix
steps.text: Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt; pour in the coldest beer you have and stir 10 seconds — lumps are correct. Overmixing develops gluten and makes it bready. Use within 10 minutes.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Dip, let excess drip, fry 2-3 minutes to deep gold, turning once. Drain on a rack. Between batches, give the oil a moment to return to temperature — dropped oil means fat-soaked batter.

steps.title: Warm the tortillas properly
steps.text: Dry comal or skillet, 20 seconds per side until they puff slightly and smell toasted. Wrapped in foil in the oven works; the microwave makes them gummy — avoid.

steps.title: Assembly line
steps.text: Tortilla, crema, cabbage, fish, pico, jalapeño slices, more crema. Two tacos per plate, lime wedges everywhere. Eat standing up for maximum authenticity.

notes: The batter waits for no one — fry immediately after mixing, and re-stir gently between batches without developing it.
Beer-free version: cold soda water works. The carbonation is what matters.
Leftover fried fish re-crisps in a 220°C / 425°F oven for 8 minutes — never the microwave.

storage: Everything stores separately: crema 5 days, slaw 1 day (it weeps), fried fish 2 days re-crisped. The assembled taco waits for exactly nobody.
